name: TD Power Systems
tagline: Genuine, accelerating export-led growth (Q1 FY27 +74% revenue / +81% PAT) on a global generator shortage, now anchored by a 10-year Siemens Energy framework -- but ~88x P/E, promoter holding down to ~27% and diluting via a Rs 600cr QIP, and weak cash conversion
business_overview: TD Power Systems manufactures generators and motors, with a growing export-led business (93% of Q1 FY27 order inflow was direct/deemed exports) increasingly tied to gas turbine and gas engine demand from AI/data-center power applications in the US, alongside distributed power and industrial applications internationally. The company is debt-free, doubling generator capacity via a new Tumkur facility, and has repeatedly raised guidance through the thread.

fundamentals_narrative: Deep read (FY26 AR + Q1 FY27 concall + Aug-2026 filings) confirms the growth is real and now adds a marquee structural anchor -- but also hardens the valuation and governance cautions. Q1 FY27 revenue +74% YoY, PAT +81%, order inflow +87% (93% exports), order book Rs 2,207cr; FY27 guidance raised to Rs 2,600cr; capacity roadmap to ~Rs 3,200cr (FY28) and >Rs 4,000cr (FY29-30) on only ~Rs 50cr/yr debottlenecking capex plus the Tumkur plant (commissioned FY26). On 13-Aug-2026 TD Power signed a 10-year Build-to-Print Manufacturing Framework Agreement with Siemens Energy for gas-turbine generator components -- a genuine step up the value-added curve and a multi-year validation of the data-centre power thesis; a separate >100MW large-generator opportunity is 'close to signing' but contributes zero FY27 revenue (18-20 month cycle). The concerns are equally concrete: the stock trades at ~88x trailing P/E and ~22x P/B; promoter holding has fallen to ~26.87% (from ~34.27% in Mar-2024) and a Rs 600cr QIP will dilute it further (the Rs 75cr promoter preferential only partly offsets); EBITDA margin is stuck at ~18-19% with no operating leverage; and cash conversion is poor -- CFO/PAT of 0.71/0.23/0.54 over three years, receivables up 70% vs 45% sales growth, which is a large part of why the QIP is needed. A trusted-roster investor (Chandragupta) separately called the Turkey margin-hit disclosure 'sketchy'. The business quality is high; the risk-reward at ~88x with a diluting, low promoter stake is not.

Naman_Gupta1 (31 loves) and manitmittal (up to 28 loves, ran an export-data-driven screening process to find TD Power) were the most-loved posts, both from the earlier bullish phase of the thread. Hemanpower's Q1 FY27 concall summary (Aug 2026) confirmed the 74-87% YoY growth acceleration and the management's refusal to size the >100MW generator opportunity until a pending announcement.

bull_case: Growth is real, current and accelerating: Q1 FY27 revenue +74% YoY, PAT +81%, order inflow +87% (93% exports), order book Rs 2,207cr; FY27 guidance raised to Rs 2,600cr
10-year Build-to-Print Framework Agreement with Siemens Energy (Aug-2026) formalises a multi-year, higher-complexity customer relationship and validates the data-centre / gas-turbine demand thesis
Genuine global shortage of generators / gas turbines / gas engines driven by AI data centres, grid stabilisation and renewables; ~93% export mix; debt-free with ROCE ~34%
Capacity roadmap to >Rs 4,000cr by FY29-30 on modest (~Rs 50cr/yr) debottlenecking capex; a >100MW large-generator opportunity near signing
bear_case: Valuation is extreme: ~88x trailing P/E, ~22x P/B, market cap ~Rs 24,278 Cr after a ~2.9x re-rating -- the multiple prices many years of 40%+ growth plus a permanently premium rating, and capitalises the Siemens / >100MW ramp that adds nothing to FY27

Promoter holding has fallen to ~26.87% (from ~34.27% in Mar-2024) and a Rs 600cr QIP will dilute it further; the Rs 75cr promoter preferential only partly offsets -- thin and shrinking skin in the game
Poor cash conversion: CFO/PAT of 0.71 / 0.23 / 0.54 over three years, receivables Rs 742cr (+70% vs 45% sales growth); working capital is scaling faster than profit and the QIP is partly to fund it
No operating leverage -- EBITDA margin flat at ~18-19% through a doubling of revenue; growth is purely volume-led on a cyclical capex/shortage that will eventually normalise
A trusted investor flagged the Turkey-contract margin-hit disclosure as 'sketchy' (no quantified liquidated damages, no root cause)
verdict_headline: Excellent business riding a real global generator shortage, now with a 10-year Siemens Energy framework -- but ~88x P/E, a low and diluting promoter stake, and weak cash conversion make the risk-reward poor
verdict_reasoning: The demand story is genuine and accelerating (Q1 FY27 +74%/+81% YoY) and the Siemens Energy 10-year build-to-print framework is a real structural upgrade -- as a business this is high quality (ROCE ~34%, debt-free, 93% exports)

But the deep read hardens the cautions: ~88x trailing P/E and ~22x P/B leave no margin of safety, promoter holding is down to ~27% and a Rs 600cr QIP dilutes further, EBITDA margin shows no operating leverage, and CFO/PAT has averaged ~0.5 with receivables up 70%

Conviction cut to Medium (from Medium-High; not floor-forced): thesis-fit stays 'neither' -- at this size and multiple a 10x in 2-3 years is implausible, and the valuation already discounts the bull case

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: At ~88x trailing P/E and ~22x P/B the market prices sustained 40-55% EPS growth for many years plus a permanently premium multiple. To justify even a 35-40x exit P/E, ~45-55% EPS CAGR over FY26-FY29 is required. Q1 FY27 (+81% PAT) and the order book support the near term, but the multiple already capitalises the Siemens Energy framework and the >100MW ramp that contribute nothing to FY27.

value_chain.theme: AI data-centre power + gas-turbine / gas-engine capacity build-out + grid stabilisation (US / Europe)
value_chain.position: tier-1 outsourced manufacturer of generators (and traction / industrial motors) to global turbine and engine OEMs -- build-to-print for the likes of Siemens Energy and INNIO; ~93% exports
value_chain.bottleneck_node: large-frame generator / rotating-equipment manufacturing capacity -- a genuine global shortage; OEMs are capacity-constrained and outsourcing to qualified vendors
value_chain.note: TD Power sits at the outsourced-manufacturing link of a real global generator shortage driven by data-centre and grid demand; the 10-year Siemens Energy build-to-print framework (Aug-2026) formalises this. But capacity is being added across the node worldwide -- including by TD Power itself -- so today's pricing environment is a shortage that will eventually normalise.

flat EBITDA margin ~18-19% -- no operating leverage

earnings_quality.normalised_note: EBITDA margin ~18-19% is roughly mid-cycle and stable, so there is no peak-margin distortion in reported earnings. The quality question is different: PAT is growing ~80% on a cyclical capex/shortage surge and only ~0.5x of it converts to operating cash; a normalised through-cycle growth rate is well below the current run-rate.

growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: YoY revenue growth: FY24 +18%, FY25 +28%, FY26 +45%, Q1 FY27 +72-74%; PAT +81% in Q1 FY27; order inflow +87% YoY (93% exports). The rate of change is clearly accelerating -- the classic re-rating setup -- but it is order / capex-cycle-driven and lumpy by nature.
growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: At ~88x trailing P/E the multiple needs ~45-55% sustained EPS CAGR for years plus a permanently premium exit multiple. The recent trend supports the near term, but this is a cyclical shortage; when the growth rate rolls from very-high to merely-high, a de-rating from ~88x is the base case.

management_quality.capital_allocation: Debt-free through the growth phase; modest capex (~Rs 50cr/yr debottlenecking + automation, plus Tumkur commissioned FY26). Now raising Rs 600cr via QIP + Rs 75cr preferential to promoters -- partly to fund working capital scaling faster than profit (receivables Rs 742cr, +70% vs 45% sales growth; CFO/PAT ~0.54). ROCE ~34%, ROE ~25%.
management_quality.capability_ladder_note: Moving from commodity generators to a 10-year build-to-print framework with Siemens Energy for gas-turbine generators, plus large-frame (>100MW) generators and hydro refurbishment -- a real step up in complexity and customer quality

four_box.note: Genuine data-centre/turbine shortage tailwind; TAM undocumented amid industry-wide capacity adds; moat neutral (build-to-print, no pricing power evidence); 88x P/E gap=priced-in

track_record.note: FY16-FY26 (screener consolidated): a decade-long turnaround -- ROCE below 15% every year FY15-FY21 and revenue shrinking FY16-FY17. Both metrics cleared only from FY22: FY22, FY24, FY25, FY26 = 4 of 11 (FY23 missed on 9.4% growth). Last 4 of 5 years clean; ROCE now 34%, OPM 18%.

quality_metrics.note: Net cash -- borrowings only Rs 18cr FY26 vs a large cash pile, so ND/EBITDA negative and interest_coverage (~40x) is the fallback metric. FCF-conv ~10% (trailing 3y CFO-capex ~Rs 80cr / EBITDA ~Rs 740cr) held down by working-capital build during 45% FY26 revenue growth. OPM expanded 12% (FY22) -> 18% (FY26); ROCE 16% -> 34%.
